ClientResponses.Response:
Hello we are sorry to hear about the issue you are experiencing lighting your grill! To ensure that you are not inadvertently activating the safety device as you turn on the grill, please use the following procedure:



-Turn all burner control knobs to OFF, including the side burner control knob if present.



-Make sure the grill lid is open. Open the LP tank valve and then wait at least 60 seconds. This will allow the hose and regulator to pressurize.



-Turn the appropriate burner control knob for your model grill to the START/HIGH position and then ignite the grill by pushing the ignition button.



-Turn each of the other burner control knobs to high, one at a time, and press the igniter button (if applicable for your model). Repeat this process until all the burners have been lit.



-Close the grill lid.



-The grill should reach approximately 500 to 550 degrees in 10-15 minutes.

If you still continue to have a hard time lighting the grill please contact our support team!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText: We have had Weber grills in the past, and chose to invest almost $500 in our newest grill. I would like to point something out, and maybe save someone else the embarrassment of going thru what we did.    The grill was assembled by the retailer. When we did the set up tests, we could not get the temp to go above 410 degrees. We called the customer service number, and a very helpful person talked us thru multiple steps, then determined we probably needed a new hose/regular set, which the company promptly sent. We replaced that, and still had problems with the temp not going high enough. We were waiting for a return call from customer service, when we figured out the problem.  The knobs to control the heat seem counter-intuitive to me. When they are turned all the way on, they are actually at "low" heat. Turning them just a very small amount turns them on "high". Once we realized that, the grill heated up quickly to 600 degrees. This was totally our fault- not any problem with the grill. The front of the grill has markings that indicate high-medium-low, and the manual also shows that. The problem was on our end- assuming that turning the knobs all the way would be "high", and partially turning them would be "low".  So, heads up! Save yourself the frustration and embarrassment we went thru!
Results.Title: Pay attention!!!!!

Bought this grill after a cheaper grill gave out after 3 or 4 years. Spent a little more for this grill based on the warranty, strong reviews, and salesperson talking up their customer service.  I've had it a year now and doesn't perform much better, if any, than my much cheaper grill and have had more issues.  Hard to regulate the temperature--even at lowest heat setting it has a hard time keeping under 400 degrees.  After 1 year of relatively light use the hose and regulator assembly began leaking.  While I assume the warranty should take care of it I've been unable to get ahold of Weber to talk to them which is the most disappointing aspect of the entire purchase as I was told their service was great.  I called and after getting the IVR message that hold times were long I chose the option for them to call me back when an agent freed up.  Waited all night without a call.  Assuming the customer service line was closed I then decided to email to inform them of both my grill issue and the customer service issue and we're at 3 and a half days with no response other than the automated email stating they received my email and would get back to me.  In the review process they ask that we not write about customer service problems but contact them instead; however, often when someone decides on a purchase their deciding based on the service and integrity of the company as much as the product.  I don't know that it makes sense to not take that into consideration in the review.  

In short, there's nothing necessarily wrong with the product but if going to have some of the same issues you have with a lesser priced grill and not receive good service/support you might as well save the money and buy the lesser grill.

Results.ReviewText:
Have been using it regularly for the last month or so that I’ve had it and there really aren’t any substantive complaints. 

I live on a small island, so corrosion is a concern that I’ll need to observe more to see how this grill withstands the salt air. My last off-brand grill only made it a couple years, so hopefully this one lasts much longer. 

Heat is good across most of the grill surface. There’s some minor variation with the rear getting a bit hotter that the middle and front. We’re up on a hill, so it’s quite windy pretty often, but the grill has started consistently on the first press of the starter. The thermometer has read almost 600f when all three burners are on high. 

The propane tank holder really only supports the metal tanks. We have fiberglass & plastic ones (to avoid corrosion) which can be clamped in the mount, but end up with the bottom of the tank resting on the wheel axle, so the gauge doesn’t display the current level. The 2nd tier rack also feels a bit dinky. Both are only minor gripes though. 

Would definitely recommend. 4.5/5
Results.Title: Great grill! Loving it so far

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: After a long process of buying and returning several damaged models from a department store, I finally bought directly from Weber. It arrived as scheduled on a pallet which was a pain in the butt to get rid of, but the assembly process was difficult. I was missing to packets of screws so for instructions that use precisely every screw in the package normally made it very difficult to put this together without issues. Most people would return and send back the grill but after everything I went through with getting this grill undamaged, I wasn't about to give up. I had to go to the hardware store and piece together the pieces I needed to assemble the grill. Let alone on my birthday. After the grill was finally assembled, I haven't been impressed with the grill plates themselves. They seem to be missing the metal hardening coating on them which gives it the ability to be non stick in the beginning. I know this wears down over time but out of the box? For a 600.00 grill I would of thought that would have been better quality.
Results.Title: Good but not great
